request.question: Survey the main technical routes to multimodal agents: interleaved visual-language learning, visual instruction tuning, embodied integration, frozen-module bridging, and tool or program composition. Explain what each route connects or trains, its representative mechanisms, and the boundary between perception, reasoning and executable actions. Cite primary papers; do not infer robotic competence from visual QA results.

Survey retrieval-augmented generation design patterns from retrieval and passage fusion to chunk-level conditioning, adaptive retrieval, hypothetical queries, recursive summaries and graph summaries. State what is retrieved and where it enters generation, and distinguish local fact lookup from global corpus synthesis. Ground the taxonomy in primary papers and identify limitations without declaring a universal winner.

Survey parameter-efficient fine-tuning families: adapters, low-rank updates, soft prompts and prefixes, activation scaling, and quantization with adapters. Explain which parameters are trained or frozen and how the mechanisms differ. Use both primary papers and the frozen versioned official PEFT guides, distinguish algorithmic claims from implementation guidance, and keep empirical comparisons tied to their experimental setting.

Survey long-context model techniques across segment recurrence, sparse attention, exact attention kernel efficiency, and positional context extension. Explain the bottleneck each addresses and whether it changes connectivity, memory traffic, or usable positions. Use primary papers and versioned official Transformers documentation to explain global attention masks and KV-cache memory tradeoffs; do not equate longer context capacity with reliable reasoning over it.

Survey speculative decoding families: separate draft models, rejection sampling, multiple decoding heads, feature-space drafting, draft-free parallel decoding, early-exit self-drafting, retrieval-based drafts and token-tree verification. Explain how proposals are produced and checked, identify which cited methods claim preservation of the target distribution, and distinguish training requirements from inference costs without pooling unrelated speedup measurements.
